title: kv-cache: improved eviction + spillover defrag heuristics to reduce fragmentation and OOMs
author: Ava Chen
description: Context: KV cache fragmentation and aggressive spillover to NVMe caused elevated OOMs and tail latency for long-context workloads. This PR updates eviction heuristics, defragmentation priorities, and paging/spillover thresholds to reduce memory churn and improve latency stability. Changes include prioritized defrag buckets, dynamic paging thresholds based on live memory pressure and sequence-length distribution, smarter spillover ordering to favor cold entries, and new telemetry for eviction/paging decisions. The goal is to reduce cache fragmentation and unnecessary NVMe spillover while preserving hit-rate and tail latencies. Checklist: - [x] Implement prioritized defrag buckets and heuristics - [x] Add dynamic paging threshold controller - [x] Add cold-entry-first spillover ordering - [x] Add metrics and dashboards (eviction_reasons, defrag_ops, spillover_rate) - [x] Add unit and integration tests + perf microbench harness - [x] Canary on dedicated pool and validate SLOs Related: ENG-3241 (KV cache defrag), ENG-3302 (spillover paging tuning), SUP-1427 (customer incident)

diff_summary: Adds defrag priority buckets, paging controller, spillover ordering and metrics. ~640 additions across runtime code, tests and docs; moderate rework of eviction paths to introduce priority queues and a new controller loop. No external API changes; config flags added under kv-cache.eviction.*
performance_results: Canary results (20% traffic on dedicated p-medium pool): 95th token latency reduced by 12%, 99th token latency reduced by 18%, KV-cache hit rate stable (+0.4%). Peak memory fragmentation measured by free-frags dropped 42%. NVMe spillover rate dropped 33% under heavy long-context workload. No regression observed on short-context microbenchmarks.
review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice work. Two questions: 1) how deterministic are defrag ops during load spikes? 2) can we add a safety throttle to avoid defrag storms?

Ava Chen: Response: Defrag ops are now bucketed and scheduled; worst-case we cap defrag work per second per shard. Added a safety throttle (kv_cache.eviction.defrag_max_ops_per_sec) and unit tests to cover bursts.
Samira Patel: Please ensure metrics include the reason for eviction (age/fragmentation/spillover) so SRE can correlate alerts. Also add labels for model_id and shard_id.
Ava Chen: Done — eviction_reason label added and model_id/shard_id tagging included in metrics. Confirmed low-cardinality for alerts by sampling model_id only at 99th percentile.
Luca Romano: Integration test flaked once in CI (ordering of spillover). Suggest deterministic seed in test. Also ping perf team about canary schedule.
Ava Chen: Fixed test by injecting deterministic RNG seed and added retry on transient FS flakiness. Perf team notified and canary scheduled for 48h.
Diego Morales: Approve after nit on log verbosity (reduced log level for defrag debug messages).

release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: prioritized defragmentation, dynamic paging thresholds, and cold-entry-first spillover ordering. Reduces fragmentation and NVMe spillover under long-context workloads; recommended to enable by default for Dedicated and Private clusters. Config knobs: kv_cache.eviction.defrag_enabled, kv_cache.eviction.defrag_max_ops_per_sec, kv_cache.paging.dynamic_threshold_enabled, kv_cache.spillover.cold_first
canary_notes: Canary ran on dedicated p-medium pool for 48h. Observed reduced tail latency and spillover rate. Rollout plan: gradual ramp to 100% over 24h after merge with close monitoring of eviction_reasons and spillover_rate dashboards.
